claims.content: The Player views the Player Statistics Window, displaying a listbox of 10 lines with each player's name, number of block movement, and time used, read from the statistic file of the game.

goal.raw_text: The Player views the Player Statistics Window, displaying a listbox of 10 lines with each player's name, number of block movement, and time used, read from the statistic file of the game.

claims.content: Player
Player statistics have been recorded in the statistic file of the game.
The statistic file of the game is available for the Player Statistics Window to read.
The Player selects the "Display" option from the Statistics menu, initiating display of the statistic window.

trigger.raw_text: The Player selects the "Display" option from the Statistics menu, initiating display of the statistic window.

claims.content: The Player selects the "Display" option from the Statistics menu.
The action "Display" displays the statistic window.
The Player Statistics Window is composed of a listbox of 10 lines.
Each line is composed of the name of a player, the number of block movement, and the time used by the player to solve the headache.
The statistics are read from the statistic file of the game.
Alternative path from main flow step 0: The Statistics menu also contains "Erase"; selecting "Erase" performs the action "Erase" and erases the statistics, see chapter 3.2.3.3.
Alternative path to main flow step 0: The Statistic Window input can be End of the game (see chapter 3.2.2.1) or menu selection.

In the end-of-game path, if the number of block movements of the current player is lower than the highest number of block movement recorded in the statistic file, the "Finish Window with Statistics" is displayed; after the Player clicks on the pushbutton "OK", the player statistics are recorded in the statistic file of the software, according to the requirement of the chapter 3.2.3.2, the "finish" window is closed, and the statistic window is displayed, see chapter 3.2.3.4.

In the end-of-game path, if the "Simple Finish Window" is displayed, after the Player clicks on the pushbutton "OK", the Simple Finish Window is closed and the statistic window is displayed, see chapter 3.2.3.4.

During the end-of-game path, after the Player clicks on the pushbutton "OK" in the Finish Window with Statistics, the player statistics are recorded in the statistic file; if the file was not correctly updated, like wrong pemissions or disk full, an error message is displayed (exception exit: error message).
The statistic window is displayed.
The Player Statistics Window is composed of a listbox of 10 lines.
Each line is composed of the name of a player, the number of block movement, and the time used by the player to solve the headache.
The statistics are read from the statistic file of the game.
